extracted.intended_audience: General readers, journalists, and nonprofit news organizations researching the Institute for Nonprofit News and its membership standards
extracted.subtask_description: Extract the criteria and standards the Institute for Nonprofit News (INN) uses or references when evaluating and admitting member newsrooms — e.g., organizational status, editorial practices, and funding transparency. Focused on INN's membership/organizational eligibility and related quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership standards include editorial independence — applicants were rejected for not meeting this standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states that in 2023, 48% of newsrooms that applied were accepted, with others not meeting membership standards like editorial independence. This is listed as an explicit criterion used in vetting membership applications; no further operational definition or examples are provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of journalism is an explicit membership standard cited by INN when evaluating applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page reports that some applicant newsrooms were rejected for not meeting 'quality of journalism' membership standards. No detailed scoring rubric or metrics are provided on the page, only that quality is a criterion in admission decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency around who funds their work
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency about funding sources is named as a membership standard — applicants lacking transparency were rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article quotes 'transparency around who funds their work' as a reason some applicants failed to meet membership standards in 2023. The page does not provide a detailed policy text or thresholds for acceptable transparency; it indicates transparency is a gating consideration for membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprofit organizational status / nature
rubrics_metrics.description: INN is described as a 'non-profit consortium of nonprofit journalism organizations,' implying members are expected to be nonprofit journalism organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes INN itself is a 501(c)(3) organization and repeatedly characterizes the network as composed of nonprofit journalism organizations. While it does not state an explicit written rule on the page that members must hold a specific tax status, the framing implies nonprofit organizational status or identity is a baseline attribute for membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on investigative and public-service journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: INN's mission and activities emphasize promoting nonprofit investigative and public service journalism, indicating a preference or evaluative orientation toward outlets working in those areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article says the organization 'promotes non‑profit investigative and public service journalism' and facilitates collaborations, training, and resources with that emphasis. Although the page does not present this as a formal checklist item, it signals that investigative/public-service orientation is central to INN's mission and likely relevant to membership and programmatic activities.
